item.research_question: How does varying tungsten concentration affect the crystal structure, microstructure, and mechanical properties (hardness, strength, ductility) of WxNbMoTa refractory high-entropy alloys fabricated via laser cladding deposition?
item.material_system: WxNbMoTa refractory high-entropy alloys with x = 0, 0.16, 0.33, 0.53 (mole fractions)
item.processing_route: Laser cladding deposition (LCD) using a coaxial LCD system with 565 W laser power, 8 mm/s scanning speed, 0.08 mm layer thickness, and 600 °C induction heating temperature; powders (45–125 μm) mixed for 4 h and dried at 120 °C for 8 h in Argon (<80 ppm O2)
item.test_conditions: Vickers microhardness (500 g load, 30 s); room temperature compression (25 °C, 0.001 s⁻¹); high-temperature compression (1000 °C, 3.5 min heating, 15 min soak, 0.001 s⁻¹ strain rate, 10⁻³ torr vacuum)
key_findings: All WxNbMoTa alloys formed a single-phase body-centered cubic (BCC) solid solution regardless of tungsten content.
Grain and dendrite sizes averaged 20 μm and 4 μm, respectively, due to rapid solidification in LCD.
Vickers microhardness increased with tungsten concentration: 459.2 ± 9.7, 476.0 ± 12.9, 485.3 ± 8.7, and 497.6 ± 5.6 Hv for x = 0, 0.16, 0.33, 0.53.
NbMoTa (x = 0) exhibited yield strength of 530 MPa and compressive strain of 8.5% at 1000 °C.
At room temperature, NbMoTa showed yield strength of 874 MPa and compressive strain of 5.8%, while W-containing alloys were brittle with compressive strengths of 840–895 MPa.
Bulk modulus increased with tungsten content: 174, 182, 186, and 192 GPa for x = 0, 0.16, 0.33, 0.53.
Spherical gas porosities in as-fabricated samples were eliminated by using molybdenum powders with higher granule density and good sphericity.
item.mechanism: Rapid solidification during laser cladding deposition (melting in 10⁻³–10⁻² s) suppresses constitutional segregation and promotes fine equiaxed grains. Tungsten addition increases lattice distortion and solid solution strengthening, raising hardness and bulk modulus but reducing ductility at room temperature. Porosity formation is attributed to adsorbed Argon gas in low-density molybdenum powder particles, not microstructure features.
item.limitations: Spherical gas porosities appeared in samples fabricated with standard molybdenum powders due to low granule density; tungsten addition reduces room-temperature plasticity, making W-containing alloys brittle.
item.future_work: The present work provides a theoretical basis for LCD manufacturing of aerospace parts of refractory HEAs with large size, complex structure, and variable composition.
quotes: The size of the grains and dendrites are 20 μm and 4 μm on average, due to the rapid solidification characteristics of the laser cladding deposition.
The increase of the tungsten concentration of WxNbMoTa has led to four results of the Vickers microhardness, i.e., Hv = 459.2 ± 9.7, 476.0 ± 12.9, 485.3 ± 8.7, and 497.6 ± 5.6.
NbMoTa alloy shows a yield strength (σb) and compressive strain (εp) of 530 Mpa and 8.5% at 1000 °C, leading to better results than traditional refractory alloys such as T-111, C103, and Nb-1Zr.
